title: Absorb one heavy slice by the factor-1 gate (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

One heavy slice fits the factor-1 gate. For integers `p ≥ 2`, `g ≥ 1`, `K ≥ 0` and `C ≥ 0`, whenever `p ≥ max(64, 4K + 2C)` and `g ceil(log2 p) ≤ p`,

```text
(p^{10})^{g-1} p^6 (1 + p^4) exp(K p - p^2)
```

is strictly below `2^{-C p}`. The exponent spends `10 g L`. One times the eighths is `8 (E + C p)`. The gate gives `80 g L = 80 · g L ≤ 80 p`. The identity `8 (2 K + C) = 4 (4 K + 2 C)` bounds the linear term by `4 p^2`. The sum is at most `-(4 p^2 - 80 p - 8)`. The polynomial `4 p^2 - 80 p - 16` equals `11248` at `p = 64` and increases by `8 p - 76`, so the exponent is at most `-C p - 1`.

At `p = 84` and `g = 12`, `g L = 84 ≤ 84` while `2 g L = 168 > 84`, and the exponent is `-6215`. The factor-2 comparison `160 g L ≤ 80 p` fails there: `13440 > 6720`. This `1` multiplies `g L`. It is not a one-bit majorant of the ceiling `9` and not a two-power majorant of `C`. The coefficient-9 monomials in #4495 still use `16 g L ≤ p`, because `9 > 8`. At `p = 2` and `g = 1` the factor holds, `g L = 1 ≤ 2`, but `p < 64`. Since `e < 3`, the slice `1088 exp(-4)` is larger than `1`.

The `g` copies under this gate stay open. The factor does not force `g < 2^L` when `L = 1`. The trailing bound `p^{10}`, the section error, and the ceiling `9 p^2` stay hypotheses. This package does not prove `||H^{-1}||_2 ≤ p^{10}`. No new κ. The selected record is `60403/20000000`. This answers the open question of #4687. It branches from fetched main and does not replay that unmerged package.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-slice-one-gate`
- [x] Prints `PASS_GAUSSIAN_SLICE_ONE_GATE` and `outcome=completed`
- [ ] Maintainer replay was not run
